quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #24
										  					
  

30 Questions • Passing Score 24

questions.question: Which road surface is most likely to be slippery in cold weather after snow or rain?

options.text: A road in a shaded area

questions.correctAnswerText: A road in a shaded area
questions.explanation: Shaded areas on roads freeze before sunny areas and thaw out later. This makes them more likely to be icy in cold, wet weather.

questions.question: When stopping on snow or ice with an Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS), you should:

options.text: Press and hold the brake pedal firmly.
Stay off the brakes and let the car drift to a stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press and hold the brake pedal firmly.
questions.explanation: With ABS, press the brake pedal firmly and keep holding it. The ABS will pump the brakes automatically, faster than you can do it manually.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Cars on the right move first.
Let cross traffic pass before proceeding.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let cross traffic pass before proceeding.
questions.explanation: This sign means you must yield. Slow down or stop to let vehicles and pedestrians crossing your path go first before you proceed.

questions.question: On a green arrow, you must:

options.text: Yield to any vehicle, bicycle, or pedestrian in the intersection.
Yield to pedestrians only in the intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield to any vehicle, bicycle, or pedestrian in the intersection.
questions.explanation: A green arrow means you can go. Turn in the direction the arrow points, but first let any vehicles, bicycles, or pedestrians in the intersection pass.

questions.question: What does a yellow left arrow traffic signal mean?

options.text: Get ready to yield to oncoming traffic.
The protected left turn is about to end.

questions.explanation: A yellow left arrow means the protected turn is ending. Prepare to yield to oncoming traffic when the arrow changes.

questions.question: If you have a sudden tire blowout, you should:
questions.explanation: When a tire blows out, hold the steering wheel firmly and keep driving straight. Slow down gradually by easing off the gas and using light brake pressure.

questions.question: If you are about to be hit from behind, you should NOT:

options.text: Let go of the steering wheel.
Press your head firmly against the head restraint.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let go of the steering wheel.
questions.explanation: If hit from behind, press your body against the seat and your head against the head restraint to prevent whiplash. Hold the steering wheel firmly and be ready to brake to avoid hitting other vehicles.

questions.question: What happens to stopping distance and crash severity when a vehicle goes faster?

options.text: They are not affected by speed.

questions.explanation: Higher speeds cause longer stopping distances and more severe crashes. Increase the distance between your vehicle and others as you drive faster.

questions.question: To avoid traffic merging from on-ramps on the right side of an interstate, you should:

options.text: Keep your speed and position the same.

questions.explanation: When you see an on-ramp ahead, move to the left lane if traffic allows. This gives entering vehicles room to merge safely.

questions.question: To make room for cars entering the freeway, you should:

options.text: Keep your speed and position the same.

questions.explanation: When possible, change lanes to create a gap for vehicles entering the freeway. If you cannot change lanes, adjust your speed to let them merge smoothly and safely.

questions.question: You see a green traffic light, but traffic is blocking the intersection ahead. What should you do?

options.text: Turn left and find another route.
Do not enter the intersection until traffic clears.
Follow other vehicles and enter the intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not enter the intersection until traffic clears.
questions.explanation: Do not enter the intersection just because the light is green if traffic is blocking your way. If you enter and the light turns red, you will block traffic crossing in the other direction. You can get a ticket for blocking an intersection.

questions.question: You are exiting the interstate. When should you start slowing down?

options.text: As you approach the deceleration lane.
Right after you enter the deceleration lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Right after you enter the deceleration lane.
questions.explanation: Keep your speed when leaving the interstate until you reach the deceleration lane. Then slow down to match the posted speed for the exit ramp.

questions.question: What is the maximum speed limit on a rural interstate unless otherwise posted?
questions.explanation: The speed limit on a rural interstate is 70 miles per hour. Always follow posted speed limit signs if they show a different speed.

questions.question: You are driving defensively when you:

options.text: Keep one car length of space between you and the car ahead.
Look only at the car directly in front of you.
Constantly scan the road ahead to spot hazards.

questions.correctAnswerText: Constantly scan the road ahead to spot hazards.
questions.explanation: Defensive driving means looking down the road for potential dangers. Do not stare only at the road right in front of your car. Look ahead and be aware of vehicles around you.

questions.question: At an intersection with a flashing red traffic light, you must:

options.text: Stop completely, yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians, then go.
Slow down and proceed with caution.
Stop completely and wait until the light is no longer red.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely, yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians, then go.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light works like a stop sign. Come to a complete stop, yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians, and proceed when it is safe.

questions.question: When dust or smoke makes it hard to see other vehicles, you should drive slowly and turn on your:
questions.explanation: Turn on your headlights whenever conditions make it hard to see other vehicles. This also helps other drivers see you.

questions.question: When you plan to pass another vehicle, you should:

options.text: Not assume the other driver will make room for you to return to your lane.
Assume the other driver will let you pass if you use your turn signal.
Assume the other driver will keep a steady speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Not assume the other driver will make room for you to return to your lane.
questions.explanation: Even if you signal, do not assume other drivers will give you space or the right-of-way.

questions.question: What does this yellow sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that traffic may merge into your lane ahead.

questions.question: In fog, rain, or snow, you should use:
questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights in fog, rain, and snow. High beams reflect off these conditions and create a bright glare that makes it harder to see.

questions.question: This sign warns of what type of condition?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. They alert you to conditions right ahead. This sign warns that another road crosses the highway ahead.

questions.question: When turning left from a two-way street onto a one-way street, where should you turn?
questions.explanation: When you turn, move from your current lane into the first available legal lane in the direction you want to go. When turning from a two-way street to a one-way street, enter the first lane.

questions.question: When entering the interstate, you find a gap in traffic, match the speed, and signal. What should you do next?

options.text: Expect other drivers to let you in since you have the right-of-way.
Wait for the lane to completely clear before merging.

questions.explanation: Find a gap in traffic, speed up to match other cars, and signal. Then merge into the gap when it is safe. Watch other traffic carefully. Do not expect other drivers to move out of your way.

questions.question: Which road surface freezes first?
questions.explanation: Bridges and overpasses freeze before other road surfaces. They can become icy even when the rest of the road is dry. Bridges freeze first and thaw last.

questions.question: A driver license is a:
questions.explanation: Driving is a privilege, not a right. All drivers must help keep roads safe. If you misuse this privilege, it can be taken away.

questions.question: Your vehicle's wheels run off the edge of the pavement. What should you do first?

options.text: Turn the front wheels slightly left to get back on the pavement.
Hold the steering wheel firmly, release the gas, and gently brake.
Brake hard and turn the front wheels sharply left.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold the steering wheel firmly, release the gas, and gently brake.
questions.explanation: If your vehicle leaves the road, grip the steering wheel tightly, take your foot off the gas, and brake gently. Slow down. Check traffic and find a safe place to return to the road. Do not jerk the wheel sharply, as this can cause you to lose control or hit other cars.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: You can travel in either direction in this lane.
You are approaching a divided highway.

questions.explanation: This sign warns that traffic flows in both directions.

questions.question: On a road with a single broken white centerline, what can you do?

options.text: You must stay in your lane.
You may cross the centerline to change lanes.
You may change lanes only from the left lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may cross the centerline to change lanes.
questions.explanation: White lines between lanes mean traffic in both lanes goes the same direction. A broken white line means you can pass another vehicle when it is safe to do so.

questions.question: When changing lanes, you should never:

options.text: Cross the centerline in an intersection.
Look over your shoulder to check your blind spot.
Check for other drivers in the same lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Cross the centerline in an intersection.
questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, look over your shoulder to check for blind spots. Watch for other drivers entering your lane. Never try to pass or change lanes in an intersection.

questions.question: When is it legal to turn left at a red light after stopping?

options.text: When turning from a two-way street onto a two-way street.
When turning from a one-way street onto another one-way street.
When you yield to all other traffic at the intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: When turning from a one-way street onto another one-way street.
questions.explanation: After a complete stop, you may turn left at a red light only when you are on a one-way street and turning onto another one-way street. Make sure there are no signs that forbid this turn.

questions.question: In bad weather, you should:
questions.explanation: In bad weather, do not slam on the brakes or make sharp, quick turns. Smooth steering and braking help you keep control of your vehicle.
